clue.text: To exhaust one's stock represents betrayal

definitions.meaning: to sell everything you have, as a shop or a show does
a treacherous abandonment of one's principles or allies

explanation.definitionFit: Selling every ticket or item is to sell all of it out, and a turncoat's treachery is likewise called by that noun.

clue.text: Old poet has old jacket, so they say

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: a spencer was a short double-breasted jacket of the 18th and 19th centuries

explanation.surface: An elderly bard turns up in an antique coat, according to gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund SPENSER wrote The Faerie Queene; the jacket is spelt with a C.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Lengthened one's dress when left in the lurch

definitions.meaning: a hem is released to make a garment longer
abandoned or failed by someone relied on

explanation.definitionFit: Hems are lengthened by releasing them, and someone abandoned has been disappointed; one phrasal verb covers both.

clue.text: Had confessed

definitions.meaning: possessed
admitted, as in ... up

explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to possess it, and to admit a fault is to own up to it.

clue.text: Major sporting event? Strike a light!

definitions.meaning: an international cricket match lasting up to five days
read literally, trying out a stick that strikes a flame

explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket fixture is a five-day contest; striking a light is trying out a matchstick.

clue.text: Instrument used to produce sherry only

parts.note: sack is an old name for sherry and other dry white wines from Spain
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A bartender explains a contraption that serves nothing but sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to produce' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance brass instrument, the early form of the trombone.

clue.text: Determined to attack

definitions.meaning: resolved, as when ... doing something
to set upon someone, as dogs do

explanation.definitionFit: Being resolved to do a thing and setting a dog upon an intruder are both expressed by one phrasal verb.

clue.text: Criminal's perverted pride at having hatched a plot

parts.note: a con is a convict, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook's twisted vanity led to scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverted' looks like it describes the criminal's character, but it signals that the letters of 'pride' are rearranged (to PIRED).
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plan secretly with others to do something wrong.

clue.text: Introduce crooner going round Russia with a popular following

indicators.note: the word for popular comes after the rest
the singer's name goes around the letter for Russia

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
R is the international code for Russia
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A singer tours Russia with a large fan base.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby is the classic crooner.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce a law or measure is to bring it in, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: 10 go roundabout with this French comic poet

indicators.note: the number goes around the word for about

parts.note: the number ten in letters
re means about or concerning
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Ten go on a roundabout with a French comic writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence was a Roman comic playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman writer of comedies in verse.

clue.text: Stretches worked by former nurses

parts.note: ex is the usual prefix meaning former
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: Exercises are done under the eye of nurses who used to work on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to lengthen or prolong it, a synonym verb in the third person.

clue.text: North African port is more pungent

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan city on the Strait of Gibraltar
the comparative of tangy, sharper in taste

explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan seaport has the same spelling as the comparative of tangy, meaning sharper in flavour.

clue.text: Singular etymologist who relishes cut and thrust

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a student of word origins is loosely a wordsman, someone skilled with words

explanation.surface: An odd scholar of words loves a lively debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut and thrust' looks like argument, but read literally it is fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer lunges and slashes with a blade, so one who enjoys cut and thrust is a fighter with a sword.

clue.text: Heathen god, cast in silver

indicators.note: the god's name has the silver set into it, as metal is cast into a mould

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A statue of a heathen deity has been cast in silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is someone outside the main world religions, a polytheist or nature worshipper.

clue.text: Tell Ronald to perform a piece of music

parts.note: Ron is the short form of the name Ronald
to do a play is to perform it

explanation.surface: Someone asks Ronald to give a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' is a link word here, an instruction to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Negotiators make them before operas start

definitions.meaning: opening approaches or proposals in talks
instrumental introductions played at the start

explanation.definitionFit: Diplomats open talks with tentative proposals, and an orchestral introduction precedes the opera; both share the noun.

clue.text: No treacle pudding? Indulgence is required!

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture of ingredients stirred together, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child complains there is no treacle pudding and must be humoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' looks like part of the dessert but signals the anagram of NO and TREACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence in the sense of putting up with others' behaviour is forbearance or acceptance.

clue.text: Frolic if there's a song in the air

definitions.meaning: play about boisterously

definitions.text: if there's a song in the air
definitions.meaning: a songbird is singing nearby, around the place

explanation.definitionFit: To romp is to fool around, and a skylark nearby means birdsong around overhead.

clue.text: Further course includes cool drink

definitions.meaning: a short course of training that brings knowledge up to date
a cold, reviving beverage

explanation.definitionFit: A top-up training course and a reviving cold beverage share the same noun, from refreshing either the mind or the body.

clue.text: Go back to the right exit

parts.note: egress is a way out

explanation.surface: Someone is told to return to the exit on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to revert to an earlier, less developed state.

clue.text: Even permitted to have a small home

parts.note: flat means even or level
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A tenant is allowed a modest place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatlet is a small apartment, typically one room.

clue.text: A little meadow seen in sunlight is divine

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small field seen in the sunshine looks heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in sunlight is divine' as the definition, but only 'divine' (to search for water with a rod) defines; 'in sunlight is' is surface padding linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to search for underground water or minerals with a forked rod, a dowser's craft.

clue.text: What soldiers eat during conflict?

definitions.meaning: read in two parts, fighting food
armed fighting between nations

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is battle food, which soldiers eat; as one word it is military hostilities.

clue.text: Never ceasing to be without purpose

definitions.meaning: continuing forever
lacking an aim or goal

explanation.definitionFit: Unending means without finish, and lacking an aim means without a goal: both senses of the same adjective.

clue.text: Old US president makes educational award

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ..., Civil War general and 18th president
money given to a student for study

explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant was the 18th American president, and a student's maintenance payment shares his surname.

clue.text: Rendered legless

definitions.meaning: coated a wall with a smooth layer of cement or lime
British slang for very drunk

explanation.definitionFit: A rendered wall has been given a smooth coat, and 'legless' is British slang for drunk, as is this slang word.

clue.text: Shame about Oriental displaying religiosity

indicators.note: the word for shame goes around the letter

parts.note: 'what a shame' means 'what a pity'
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: It is sad to see an Eastern visitor making a show of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, as religiosity is.

clue.text: Mild rebuke otherwise made by teacher

parts.note: tut is a click of mild disapproval
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or else'

explanation.surface: A teacher's gentle telling-off is otherwise done.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or instructor.

clue.text: English angler ordered to elaborate

indicators.note: these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An English fisherman is told to go into more detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as an instruction to the angler, but it signals rearranging the letters of 'angler'; 'to elaborate' means to enlarge on a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on a point is to expand or amplify it, as in enlarging on a theme.

clue.text: A German in bizarre gear causes dire offence

indicators.note: the A and G go inside the word for bizarre

parts.note: outré means unconventional, as bizarre clothing is

explanation.surface: A German tourist in strange clothes upsets people badly.
explanation.walkthrough: OUTRÉ is a French borrowing for eccentric or outlandish; A and G sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrage people is to shock and offend them deeply, a verb in the third person matching 'causes'.

clue.text: Please make reparation

definitions.meaning: to give pleasure or contentment
to pay off a debt or claim fully

explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to content them, and to settle a claim or debt fully is the older legal sense of the same verb.

clue.text: Vessels seen by small numbers flanking Northern river

indicators.note: the word for small numbers sits either side of the river

parts.note: tens are small numbers, the column after units
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Boats are watched by a few people standing along a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded dish for serving soup, so these serving dishes are vessels.
